title: Hosted netns recurrence has two root causes
body: Read-only RCA from GitHub runs 33228376245, 33228084721, 33226431905, and 33226227591 plus current tree. Runs 33228084721 and 33226431905 show exact daemon error `Error response from daemon: bind-mount /proc/<transient-pid>/ns/net -> /var/run/docker/netns/<id>: no such file or directory` while starting `umd-sandbox-runner-1`; random PID/netns IDs and daemon origin identify hosted Docker/Moby namespace lifecycle race/runner limit, not Compose DNS/topology. Latest run 33228376245 starts db/api/worker/Hatchet and fails first at Docker E2E step 8 with `sandbox-runner=restarting`; downloaded diag-final/log-sandbox-runner.txt proves custom seccomp denies `statx`/`fsmount` (`operation not permitted`), while `getcwd() failed: Operation not permitted` and `/usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh: 24: Cannot fork` repeat. `compose-ps.txt` shows API/db/worker/engine/dashboard running, migrate/admin exited 0, sandbox restarting. Current workflow has bounded netns retry and reconciliation, but must not treat all failures as transient. Plan K P3-S3 (plan lines 51-62) requires full moby default syscall surface plus bwrap additions; Task/plan require complete native Compose topology, no skips/DinD/socket mounts/fake readiness. Safe remediation: retain native topology/gates; use narrowly matching bounded retry and fresh reconciliation for exact daemon error; fix seccomp from complete moby default baseline plus required bwrap syscalls, retaining nonprivileged controls; verify sandbox env and real execution. Required proof is pushed-SHA hosted evidence: no daemon bind-mount errors/restart loops, exact service state/inspect, zero seccomp EPERM, all live/boundary JUnit tests executed with skipped=0, real workflow registration/callback rows and HTTP/restart/persistence PASS markers. No code changed.

title: Root cause: hosted JWT minted for internal tenant with no scheduler partition
body: Run 33229130339 / Docker 99038602321 exact root cause: validation.yml lines 277-285 discovers the first Hatchet tenant with ORDER BY "createdAt" LIMIT 1, which is the system `internal` tenant, not the user `Default` tenant. diag-final/umd-dump.sql proves internal tenant 8d420720-ef03-41dc-9c73-1c93f276db97 has schedulerPartitionId=NULL and workerPartitionId=NULL, while Default tenant 707d0855-80ab-4e1f-a156-f1c4546cbf52 has both partitions populated. APIToken `default` and the active `umd-worker`, nine workflows, and all 45 v1_task/v1_queue_item rows are tenant 8d420...; SchedulerPartition/Controller/TenantWorkerPartition heartbeats exist only for Default's assigned partitions. Thus engine persisted submissions and worker registration but scheduler had no tenant partition assigned for the token's internal tenant, so no assignment/runtime/event/callback and UMD stage rows stayed zero. Root cause is hosted tenant provisioning/JWT selection, not product runner, DB DSN, callback, token validity, or run_workflow shape. Remediation: select the actual user/default tenant deterministically after quickstart (e.g. query tenant with non-null schedulerPartitionId/workerPartitionId and fail if not exactly one; or use the tenant id returned/created by setup), mint JWT for that tenant, then assert token tenant == worker/workflow tenant and tenant partition IDs are non-null before live tests. Preserve real gates; no skips/doubles/fake readiness. Falsifier: rerun exact pair with JWT for Default tenant; dump must show submitted task tenant = 707d..., scheduler/worker partition IDs non-null, queue items transition to assigned/running and worker logs show callback; if still queued, investigate next-level scheduler pair issue.

title: Confirmed Plan K tenant gate ordering root cause

title: Confirmed RCA: callback-time evidence snapshot creates keys and live-shape count is global
body: Definitive run 33237228740 RCA. live-dup: Hatchet submits each stage as an independent workflow (runner.py:220-245); no enforced dependency barrier in HatchetWorkerFactory.start (hatchet.py:520-529). First BASIC callback starts at worker log 05:56:50.868 (log-worker.txt:25-29), while FORMAT completes at 05:56:50.900; its stage_run is created 05:56:50.883866 with key 000...81c3 (dump umd-dump.sql:10823), so handler.py:346-348's job-scoped committed_evidence_refs sees no completed FORMAT and computes the empty-evidence key. Second BASIC starts 05:56:51.288 (log-worker.txt:52-54), after FORMAT completed; it resolves FORMAT evidence and computes a different key 000...95bb, creating row e751... at 05:56:51.300976 (dump:10830). Lookup is not per Hatchet run: job_repository.py:167-193 filters only job_id/upstream stage/complete. Executor key is full manifest material including evidence (manifest.py:167-194), while claim dedups only that computed key (stage_repository.py:98-156). Thus claim/UNIQUE works; unstable callback-time lineage is the defect. live-shape does NOT have 16 rows/events: _poll_until diagnostics are global; its predicate is job-filtered (tests/test_hatchet_live.py:278-290), and dump has exactly 6 live-shape stage_run rows (10831-10836) and 6 StageCompleted events seq 14,15,16,19,20,22 (10763-10767,10775,10777). The global 16 = live-dup's 10 + live-shape's 6. v1_task rows 12279-12287 are exactly 9 live-shape tasks, retry_count=0; worker log 75-101 has one start/finish each. Ack payloads 11842,11851,11868,11874,11877,11884,11886 show exactly three replayed (INGEST/BASIC/CURRENT) and six real executions. Distinct keys/rows/events prove no same-key insert failure or callback retry. Partial replay is caused by cross-job mismatch: job_id is excluded from idempotency material (manifest.py:172-174), but committed_evidence_refs is scoped to the new job_id, so a new job cannot see upstream rows committed under live-dup; it rekeys FORMAT and descendants while replaying stages whose keys need no local upstream refs. Fix is NEEDS_PLAN: coordinate real dependency barriers/lineage snapshot before callbacks and redesign committed-ref lookup around canonical source+universe(+segment/rerun lineage), preserving evidence-based rekey semantics; add hosted delayed-upstream and cross-job duplicate assertions. Do not merely add a natural-key constraint, ignore evidence, or alter tests.

Failing predicates are already job-scoped: tests/test_hatchet_live.py:266-275 filters stage_run by job_id, and :278-290 filters StageCompleted payload->>'job_id'. _poll_until diagnostics at :351-357 are global, causing misleading 10/16 suffixes. title: RCA: parent_id is wrong cross-workflow barrier field on pinned Hatchet
body: Hosted run 33240528692 proves the Plan K native barrier implementation did not gate dispatch. Installed SDK 1.38.1 maps TriggerWorkflowOptions.parent_id to TriggerWorkflowRequest.parent_id (clients/admin.py:223-228); parent_step_run_id separately maps to parent_task_run_external_id. The runner passed each prior workflow_run_id as parent_id (src/umd/jobs/runner.py:220-260), but dump v1_task_20260829 rows all have parent_task_external_id/parent_task_id NULL (umd-dump.sql:12153-12190), and WorkerAssignEvent is empty (10078-10079). Worker log shows dependent FORMAT and BASIC callbacks started before INGEST finished (log-worker.txt:19-28, 97-99), with fail-closed MissingRequiredEvidenceError cascade. Therefore parent_id alone is lineage/parent-workflow metadata here, not the required step dispatch barrier. SDK has real intra-workflow DAG dependencies: @workflow.task/@workflow.durable_task accept parents (runnables/workflow.py:1412-1458, 1701-1760), Task.to_proto emits parents (runnables/task.py:495-510). For separate one-task durable workflows, the native cross-workflow candidate is parent_step_run_id (actual upstream step-run external ID), optionally paired with parent_id; this must be wired/proved with persisted parent_task_external_id/id and child ASSIGNED/RUNNING only after parent completion. Current plan P2-S8/P2-S14 wording must be amended from parent_id/parent workflow id to parent_step_run_id/step-run barrier. Canonical evidence selection remains correct and fail-closed. Proof latent bug: v1_task_runtime is ephemeral/empty after terminal callbacks, while v1_tasks_olap.latest_worker_id is populated and statuses show actual assignment; proof's assigned=runtime.worker_id query is wrong (umd-dump.sql:12578-12579, 12626-12670), despite worker callbacks proving execution. No files modified.

title: Final RCA: parent_id cannot encode hosted durable barrier
body: Run 33240528692 is DIAGNOSED. runner.py:220-260 passes upstream workflow-run IDs as parent_id; hatchet.py:212-265 correctly serializes them through SDK 1.38.1 as TriggerWorkflowRequest.parent_id. Pinned server v0.105.2 newTriggerOpt resolves parentTask only from parent_task_run_external_id (SDK parent_step_run_id), while parent_id is parent workflow-run context; durable DAG completion barriers are encoded by workflow-definition parent matches/DagParentTaskRunIds, not independent non-DAG durable submissions. Hosted v1_task_20260829 rows 12154-12198 show 45/45 input={} (projection/payload representation; callback reached manifest handler, so input loss is not proven) and all parent_task_external_id/id/inserted_at/child fields NULL, is_durable=t, is_dag_orchestrator=f. Worker log 19-28 proves FORMAT starts at 07:21:10.452 before INGEST completes, then fail-closed MissingRequiredEvidenceError. _make_handler lines 374-402 performs canonical_evidence_refs at 387-392 before executor.run, and job_repository.py:218-266 correctly selects COMPLETE upstream or raises; no lookup defect. v1_task_runtime is ephemeral: dump 12575-12579 empty, but OLAP 12626-12670 has terminal statuses and latest_worker_id; proof script 191-205 is a secondary false-negative. Local delayed test 1883-1927 uses _RecordingClient 175-218, so verifies seam/callback fail-closed only, not engine scheduling. Fix complexity NEEDS_PLAN. Native parent-task barrier is not expressible as currently implemented; no hosted evidence proves parent_step_run_id alone gates independently submitted durable non-DAG runs. Minimal correct alternative: one Hatchet workflow/DAG definition with durable tasks and parents derived directly from STAGE_DEPENDENCIES, one workflow submission, or supported Hatchet durable child/DAG orchestration—not independent one-shot runs with parent_id, polling, callback resubmission, or a second scheduler. title: Plan T source-C scoped read root cause: post-filter pagination truncation
body: Hosted run 33445148353 dump proves C membership is correctly persisted and string-compatible: current_state row 10677 entity:canonical:b43708aa7ab960d2 CANONICAL_IDENTITY has memberships.source_ids=[c218a6fe-075c-42ea-9c1f-7d816b8fc5b3] and work_ids=[e2f8...]. Failure request is dashed c218a6fe-075c-42ea-9c1f-7d816b8fc5b3. QueryService._in_membership_scope (query.py:308-328) compares string set intersection correctly. The defect is pagination order: _entities helper passes only source_id for scoped calls, so API default limit=20; QueryService general entities branch (query.py:258-271) calls _entity_ordered -> _entity_rows, which applies LIMIT 2*(20+0)+4=44 before Python membership filtering. Unscoped helper requests limit=100 (204-row fetch), sees C Mara. Thus no dashless/dashed mismatch, missing work_id, stale cursor, merge/split, or C ESTABLISH loss. Hermetic green is misleading only because its smaller/less-populated state keeps C candidate within the capped fetch, or its test path uses fewer rows; same QueryService filtering logic is not tested at sufficient cardinality. Minimal fix candidate: make membership-scoped ENTITY retrieval filter before pagination (prefer SQL JSONB membership predicate or fetch all identity candidates when non-empty scope; ensure total/pagination are computed after scope), including general/alias branches. title: Final diagnosis: live-only appearance is cardinality-sensitive query pagination bug
body: Final root cause for hosted run 33445148353: QueryService.entities general/ref branch fetches a bounded raw candidate page before membership filtering. API list_entities default limit=20 (entities.py:63), _entity_rows uses LIMIT (limit+offset)*2+4 = 44 (query.py:330-353). Scope is then applied in Python after _entity_ordered (query.py:258-271). Hosted dump has 104 canonical candidate rows sorted by entity_ref. A Mara entity:canonical:4a8... is candidates 24/25 and is fetched; C Mara entity:canonical:b437... is candidates 68/69 and is not fetched. Yet C is valid: EntityResolved ESTABLISH seq329 (dump semantic_event row 28369) and current_state row 10677 both carry exact dashed source c218a6fe-075c-42ea-9c1f-7d816b8fc5b3; unscoped limit=100 fetches all and displays it. Hermetic green is cardinality masking (fresh isolated DB, few candidates), not evidence live DAG produced malformed membership. Recommended fix: make ENTITY membership scope part of candidate selection before bounded pagination—prefer an SQL/relational membership predicate; minimally when scope exists fetch/filter/dedupe all identity candidates before slicing (and ensure total is post-scope), with regression coverage at >44 candidates plus live boundary.
